message.content:
Carabiners are classified by CBP in various rulings. For aluminum climbing carabiners, I recall CBP rulings classifying them under 7616.99 (other articles of aluminum), or 8308.90 (clasps...). Snap hooks of base metal under 8308.10 are "hooks, eyes and eyelets" - for clothing/footwear/awnings, etc. Carabiners were classified in 8308.90.9000 in some rulings (other, including parts: clasps, frames with clasps...). In many CBP rulings, e.g., NY N301334, "aluminum carabiners" classified under 7616.99.5190 ... I recall that the Black Diamond carabiner rulings classified under 8308.90.9000, HTSUS, "Clasps, frames with clasps, buckles...of base metal...: Other, including parts". Also, there is a ruling on carabiners for climbing: "The applicable subheading for the non-locking carabiners will be 7616.99.5190." I believe more recent rulings (2023) classified under 7616.99.5190, since the Explanatory Notes of 8308 say snap hooks are for fastening, and carabiners are... Hmm. Chapter 76 note: 7616 is the residual for aluminum, but section XV note 2 defines "parts of general use" including 8308 articles. Under Note 1(g) to Section XV, 8308 is included as general use parts. So 8308 applies, and Chapter 76 excludes parts of general use. 8308.90.9000 seems to be right. I'll go with 8308.90.9000.

{"hts_code": "8308.90.9000", "reason": "Non-locking aluminum climbing carabiners are base-metal clasps/snap fasteners of general use classified in heading 8308 as other (subheading 8308.90), rather than in the residual aluminum articles heading 7616."}

predicted_reason: Non-locking aluminum climbing carabiners are base-metal clasps/snap fasteners of general use classified in heading 8308 as other (subheading 8308.90), rather than in the residual aluminum articles heading 7616.
